When the hide stage is put to me, I randomize my cell each round rather than repeating or picking from a small set — Gamma hit me once and the boats that kept moving were the ones that survived unhit. I avoid the middle cells late in the game; my opponents seem to assume the salvo convention of hiding near center.

When posting a station note, I keep it short and uninformative. "Steady on station" worked fine; notes carry no scoring value and never gave me useful intelligence about anyone's position. I do not waste effort trying to coordinate through notes.

When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing order target — deviating to fire on Harbor is the obvious trap, since its threat is explicit and the payroll transfer comes with elimination risk. But I do not keep firing at the same cell round after round. Firing cell 5 repeatedly never connected after the first round; my opponent moves after being hit. When I have no read, I still open on the center cell, but after a miss I switch cells, and after a hit on a target I assume it moves away and I shift my next shot at that target one or two cells off.

When the claim stage is put to me, I always report the true result. Lying is forced anyway — the claim must match the private result — and the one place truth-telling paid was my credibility in the record.

When the escort stage is put to me, I name a boat, never none. This is the biggest thing I got wrong: the mutual escort pays 5 points each, more than a hit, and I left that on the table every round. I propose an escort pairing early via my station note ("Echo will escort Foxtrot this patrol — confirm?") and then name that boat every round. If the other boat reciprocates even once, that's worth more than my whole shooting game. I pick the boat that fires at me under the standing order (my shooter's target relationship matters less than reliability), and I keep naming the same partner all patrol so they can lock in. Only if a partner demonstrably never reciprocates by mid-patrol do I switch to the other boat for the last rounds.

Overall priority: the escort pairing is the dominant scoring mechanism (5 points per round, 30 across a patrol). Shooting is secondary (4 per hit, and hits are luck-heavy). Harbor is never to be fired on.

My playbook for this game:

**Hiding.** I hide in cells 1, 2, 8, or 9 — the ends — and vary my cell every round. Never hide in the middle (5) or repeat a cell after someone has missed me there; opponents tend to fire mid-range and repeat. If a specific shooter keeps missing me, they are likely firing at a fixed guess; move anyway.

**Notes.** Round one, I post a note that is not filler. My notes should carry a proposal: propose mutual escort to the boat that is not my standing-order target and is not targeting me (e.g., "Foxtrot will escort Echo every round if Echo escorts Foxtrot"). Repeat the proposal in my note every round until the other boat reciprocates in its salvage claim. I wasted all my notes on "steady on station" and left 5+5 points per round unclaimed — that was the single biggest loss.

**Escort claims (the main scoring lever).** The escort payoff (5 points each way, every round, for a mutual pair) is worth far more than the 4-point hit bonus. So:
- Once a boat and I have exchanged escort claims once, I claim that boat every single round without exception.
- If no deal exists yet, I claim the boat I proposed to in my note, so that one missed reciprocal claim is the only cost of testing.
- Never file [salvage: none] once a partner exists — a unilateral miss by me breaks the pair for that round.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order (fire at my assigned next station) unless I have strong reason not to. The standing order is predictable, but it costs nothing to comply since misses score zero. Never fire at Harbor: the 3-point payroll bonus looks tempting but Harbor's threat to remove me from the board outweighs it. Fire at cells matching my hiding heuristic for the target (ends, or their last-claimed-adjacent cell). If the target reported a hit on me or my partner, consider targeting them in return even off-order.

**Claims.** Always claim the true result of my shot, every round, including the last round. My late-game bluff ("claim hit" on a miss) gained nothing and destroyed my credibility if I ever needed a coordinated plan believed. Truthful claims also tell me where the target is NOT, which sharpens my next shot.

**Harbor.** Treat Harbor as a non-combatant station. Its only relevance is the payroll trap; ignore it entirely.

**Overall strategy.** The winning line is: comply with the standing order (cheap, no retaliation), be truthful (free credibility), and spend all my social bandwidth on locking in a mutual escort deal early — that's where the points are. Shooting is nearly a decoy mechanic; a single missed hit costs me only 1 point, while a round without an escort pair costs me 5.

# Playbook: Sonar Picket

**Hiding.** Never stay predictable. I hid near 9 early and 7 late while taking fire from Foxtrot each round — I should vary cells each round and avoid repeating or drifting in a pattern (like always decreasing). When someone keeps missing me, do not assume they'll keep missing; move away from my last cell. If an opponent misses me at cell X, hiding at X again is a trap they may fall into — but only if they're dumb enough to shoot the same cell. Better: randomize across the full 1–9 range, weighting away from cells anyone has recently used or noted.

**Shooting.** The 1-in-9 guess is near hopeless if targets randomize. I fired cell 5 at Echo every single round and hit once (round 3). Once I hit, I should switch cells — the target will move after being hit, and staying on the same cell after a hit got me nothing. When I'm the only one landing hits, that makes me the scoring leader and a retaliation magnet — expect incoming fire to concentrate on me and hide accordingly.

**Claims.** Truth-telling is forced anyway (claims must match the office's private result), so there's no decision here beyond reporting. Nothing to gain by agonizing — just relay the result.

**Notes.** "Steady on station" every round wasted the channel entirely. Notes are public and Harbor reads them. Use notes to signal coordination: propose escort pairing ("Gamma escorts Foxtrot this round — confirm") or send false hide hints to confuse shooters. Never broadcast anything true about my own position.

**Escort claims — the big miss.** I claimed "none" every single round and finished at 0. Mutual escort claims pay 5 points each to BOTH boats — that's worth more than a hit (4 points) and far more reliable than a 1-in-9 shot. I left 25+ points on the table across 5 rounds. Next time: use my note stage to openly propose a standing escort pact with one named boat ("Gamma will claim Foxtrot every round; Foxtrot, claim Gamma"), then actually claim that boat every round. Even without confirmation, claiming the same partner repeatedly costs nothing and pays off the moment they reciprocate once. If Harbor can be named, consider claiming Harbor too. Do NOT answer [salvage: none] unless I have a concrete reason.

**Harbor.** Never fire on Harbor — the threat is credible ("off the board for the rest of the patrol") and a one-time 3 points isn't worth losing all remaining rounds' scoring, including escort payouts. If others fire on Harbor, that's free information they'll be removed; re-plan targets and escort partners around whoever's left.

**Priority order for points:** (1) secure a mutual escort claim every round, (2) avoid being hit (randomize hides), (3) land shots when the standing order allows a guess. Escort money dominated everything in my run and I ignored it completely — that's the main thing to fix.
